narr: A strong upper low slowly pivoted towards Arkansas from Texas on the 28th. Abundant moisture streamed into the region ahead of the system, resulting in efficient rainfall rates over the northern half of the state once showers and thunderstorm initiated. Rainfall amounts of three to six inches was not uncommon, leading to flash flooding and river flooding.
ev: Numerous low water crossings throughout the county are flooded with many being barricaded.
A portion of Bohannon Road, just south of Highway 254 West, was flooded.
Massey Mountain Road was flooded from heavy rain.
Highway 64 was closed due to high water over the road. Two swift water rescues occurred, one on Hwy. 359 near Piney Creek, and the other on Hwy. 164 near Horsehead Creek.
Water was covering portions of Hwy. 95 West.

A campground manager reported the Spring River was out of its banks through Hardy, high water in River Bend Park, Loberg Park, and Hardy City RV Park Campground. One RV was washed away by the water. No injuries.
Water was reported to be over portions of Hwy. 359.
Social media video showed high water moving over Talley Cemetery Rd. bridge between Jessieville and Hot Springs Village.
